subject: dragonfly
pitch: An emperor dragonfly hovering above a pond. A long, slim abdomen in electric blue with black markings down its back, an apple-green thorax, huge wraparound turquoise eyes, and four glassy wings with a fine net of dark veins and a faint golden sheen, held flat and wide. Six thin legs are tucked under it.
reasoning:
I should stick to a modest, documented subset of the SDK's building blocks—joints, chains, sweeps, parts, sticks, surfaces, membranes, rings, and painting helpers—since overusing undocumented features risks breaking the module.

Now I'm figuring out the dragonfly's scale: real emperor dragonflies have roughly a 110mm wingspan and 80mm body length, so I'll keep real-world proportions (abdomen ~0.08m, thin ~0.004m radius) rather than stylizing up, placing the hovering body around y=0.25 to read as airborne above the pond. I'm laying the body along the Z axis with the head forward near z=0.05 and the abdomen trailing back toward z=-0.09.

Setting up body chain and joints...

For placing dorsal markings, I'm figuring out how to get a surface point via b.surface(abdSweep).nearest(p), then stick small flat shapes like a tiny sphere onto that hit point since I'm unsure how stick geometry aligns to the surface axis.

For the wings, I'm planning membranes between a leading and trailing edge defined as point arrays, with roots anchored near the top of the thorax and tips extending outward at roughly equal spacing on both sides, and I'm guessing veins can be built from thin rod primitives connecting points across the membrane, though I'm unsure of the exact radius parameter so I'll fall back to a generic part call if needed.

I'm also laying out a vein network of several longitudinal lines per wing plus cross veins interpolated between them, using a pale membrane color with dark vein tones, and now I'm sketching the leg structure as jointed chains (coxa, femur, tibia) tucked beneath the thorax for each of the six legs.

For the eyes, I'm making them huge turquoise wraparound spheres positioned at the sides of a small head, essentially letting the eyes dominate the head shape.

For the thorax, I'm going apple-green using a stretched ellipsoid sphere with scale adjustments, maybe adding faint oblique stripes later.

For the abdomen, I'm segmenting it into ten tapering sections with alternating electric-blue coloring and black dorsal markings, mimicking an emperor dragonfly's pattern, using sweeps along the z-axis for each segment.

Thinking through how the abdomen should bend — keeping it horizontal for a hovering pose rather than drooping — and deciding to build it as a chain of joints so each tapered sweep segment follows the curve naturally using plain points assigned to nearest bones.

I'm working out the abdomen's segment geometry: defining z-positions and tapering radii from thicker near the thorax down to narrow at the tail, scaled up slightly for visual punch, then planning dorsal black marking capsules along the top of each segment.

For the wings, I'm placing the forewing root and leading edge points relative to the thorax, setting up the proportions for a wide, flat wingspan typical of a hovering dragonfly.

Adding wing veins and cross-vein geometry...

Picking a pale golden membrane color for the wings, then moving to the legs: six legs total, each a three-point chain of hip, knee, and foot, positioned at front, mid, and rear z-coordinates with the knee tucked forward and foot pulled back underneath the thorax.

Defining the mirrored leg chains...

For the head, I'm placing two overlapping turquoise eye spheres near the top, considering a darker accent color for the face area, and settling on an apple-green tone for the thorax.

I'm working out the thorax geometry -- an elongated, scaled sphere positioned slightly forward on the body -- and thinking about adding darker stripe accents, though I may skip that detail since the thorax is a raw mesh surface without easy attachment points.

I'm setting up the root joint for the body roughly a quarter meter above the ground to give it a natural hovering height over the pond, and deciding how many joint chains I actually need versus keeping the rig simpler by handling wings separately from the legs and abdomen chain.

For dorsal markings, I'm figuring out how to query the nearest point on each body segment's surface so I can place small decorative marks accurately along the back.

Now I'm defining the color palette -- electric blue for the main body segments, a darker navy for the tail club, black for small stripe accents, plus green and turquoise tones -- and planning to use small flat tiles instead of spheres for the markings since sticking parts don't support scaling. I'm also deciding to add small spheres at each segment joint to smooth over any visible seams in the abdomen sweep.

Setting up the dragonfly build function...

Still placing joint spheres and markings...

Plotting wing coordinates...

Adding cross-vein netting...

Writing vein sweep geometry...

Setting leg positions per segment with varying z-depths for front, mid, and rear legs, then tapering abdomen segment radii from thicker near the thorax down to a narrow tail with a slight club swell at the tip, keeping total body length around 0.13 units.

I'll finalize abdomen segment spacing at roughly 0.0082 units, giving a body length close to the real emperor dragonfly proportions, and darken the last two tail segments to a deeper blue for the club marking while placing dorsal box markings on each segment surface using nearest-point projection.
